scope: Prospective matched total profiling-plus-inference cost comparison on validated4B/H200/b64, not steady-state inference gain.
primary_endpoint: Total measured elapsed seconds through16 held-out test passes (3072 requests). Candidate must reduce time by at least10percent versus each cheap control in both orders for a positive current-setting claim. All endpoints reported.

methods.screen_confirm: One forced shared engine screens1..8. Select top2 by summed timed profiling seconds, then profile both natively and choose minimum native time.
methods.native_pair: Profile3 and8 natively, choose minimum timed seconds.
methods.full_native: Profile1..8 natively, choose minimum timed seconds.

accounting: Actual same-host monotonic wall clock from pipeline start through inference milestones. Includes subprocess imports, engine startup, all profiling warmups/timing, stage teardown, selection and deployment startup. Deployment first pass is counted useful inference, with no excluded deployment warmup. Queue time and common freshAR correctness-reference cost excluded; reference cost reported separately. Per-stage files and correctness-check overhead remain included.
cache_condition: Existing on-disk caches from v72 native/ar and v105 forced. All methods reuse identical per-role/width caches, with fresh engine processes. Opposite method orders reveal order sensitivity. Not a cold-start or guaranteed identical cache-residency experiment.
selection_safety: Only profile data enter ranking; selected width persisted before held-out deployment. Tie chooses smaller width. No hyperparameter tuning after results.
freshness: Held-out test split from v103 now allocated to this frozen4B comparison. Its outcomes cannot later be advertised as untouched for another method. v103 eightB sweep still uses profile split only.
limitations: One4B model/GPU and batch64; no generalization claim from this comparison.
192unique held-out prompts repeated16times; repeated requests are not independent prompt samples.
Two timing orders are not a population confidence interval.
Shared-engine selection uses untrained heads only as required runtime scaffolding; forced full verification ignores them.
A win against full native sweep alone is insufficient if cheaper controls outperform the candidate.
No novelty claim for generic multi-fidelity screening; this is a practical method feasibility test.
